attacks.claim: Signatures cover only timestamp and body with no nonce or seen-delivery record, so a captured signed delivery can be replayed for up to 5 minutes. Because upserts are keyed on (device_id, measured_at), a replay can only restore previously signed values, which the context already treats as harmless.
attacks.evidence: TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300 ... expected = hmac.new(secret, timestamp.encode() + b"." + body, ...)

Unauthenticated requests read the full body (up to the proxy's 1 MB cap), compute HMAC over it, and resolve get_db before any auth check. This is bounded by the proxy cap but still gives unauthenticated callers cheap per-request work.

After deploy, a wrong or missing vendor secret causes every delivery to return 401 with only warning logs and no alert or metric. The artifact does not say whether PlugCloud retries 4xx responses, so readings may be lost silently. Also, Settings now requires the secret, so a missing value stops the whole service from starting, not just the webhook.
attacks.evidence: log.warning("plugcloud webhook rejected: %s", exc) ... plugcloud_secret: SecretStr (no default)
